items.title: Targeted by U.S., Armed Group Strikes Back in Colombia
items.summary: American forces are helping Colombia and Venezuela hunt the ELN. This weekend, the group attacked a Colombian military base with drones, officials said.
items.full_text:
Title: Targeted by U.S., Armed Group Strikes Back in Colombia - The New York Times

URL Source: https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/08/world/americas/colombia-drone-attack-eln.html

Published Time: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 01:03:39 GMT

Markdown Content:
A decades-old rebel group launched a deadly attack on a military base in Colombia on Saturday, killing at least three soldiers and injuring more than a dozen, Colombian officials said.

The attack, carried out by explosives-laden drones, was the largest retaliatory strike against Colombian forces since the country’s new president took office in August and declared an all-out offensive on trafficking groups, experts said.

Officials blamed the National Liberation Army, better known by its initials in Spanish, ELN, for the attack, which took place in Santa Rosa del Sur, a town around 100 miles from the Venezuelan border in northern Colombia.

The United States has been helping Colombia and Venezuela target the ELN. On Oct. 30, [U.S. forces assisted the Venezuelan Army](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/03/world/americas/us-venezuela-strike-eln-drug-trafficking.html) in a drone attack on the group in Venezuela, providing intelligence and the drones.

The ELN is Colombia’s oldest surviving leftist rebel group and a known cocaine trafficker that controls territory in both Colombia and Venezuela.

Colombia’s president, Abelardo De La Espriella, denounced the attack on the military base, which came the day after authorities [arrested](https://www.ejercito.mil.co/ejercito-nacional-impacta-estructura-de-mando-y-finanzas-del-eln-tras-la-captura-de-alias-carrito-en-el-sur-de-bolivar) an ELN leader expert in illicit finances, known as Carrito, in the area. The president pledged to continue hunting the traffickers.

“We won’t back down by even a millimeter!” he said in [a social media message](https://x.com/ABDELAESPRIELLA/status/2119268795873202454?a=igX-1DyxkanzcmbbDzM&s=20) Saturday night. He later [posted the photos](https://x.com/ABDELAESPRIELLA/status/2119427067372532091?a=PtcVkhTUV7oze5CaDDk&s=20) of the three fallen soldiers.

Mr. De La Espriella also [blamed the ELN](https://x.com/ABDELAESPRIELLA/status/2119410347585028261?a=Vx7bkDuUKxAfUMkm0Gk&s=20) for bomb threats on Colombian media outlets. Employees of Caracol, a major broadcaster, [evacuated their headquarters](https://www.eltiempo.com/bogota/atencion-evacuan-instalaciones-de-caracol-television-por-amenaza-de-bomba-esto-se-sabe-3599325) in Bogotá, the capital, on Saturday.

For decades, Colombian groups including the ELN have struck energy infrastructure and civilian targets in response to attacks by the military.

Until recently, the Colombian authorities were acting largely on their own in [combating the ELN](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/01/16/world/americas/trump-petro-colombia-eln-cocaine.html). They said they could not defeat the group because its fighters frequently escaped to Venezuela, where officials allowed the group to operate openly.

Image

President Abelardo De La Espriella of Colombia speaking last week in Cúcuta, a city on the border of Colombia and Venezuela, where the ELN is entrenched.Credit...Lucas Molet/Reuters

On a visit to Colombia in September, Secretary of State Marco Rubio [told reporters](https://www.state.gov/releases/office-of-the-spokesman/2026/09/secretary-of-state-marco-rubio-remarks-to-press-14) that the ELN should not be allowed to operate “with impunity” in Venezuela anymore, and said the issue had been raised with the country’s interim leader, Delcy Rodríguez.

The joint strike on the ELN on Oct. 30, which took place in Venezuela’s Apure region, near the Colombian border, killed around two dozen people, according to Fundaredes, a Venezuelan rights group that alerted the public to the attack after speaking to survivors and local residents.

It was not clear whether the strike had targeted ELN leadership. Officials in Venezuela did not respond to questions.

Around the time of the attack in Venezuela, Mr. De La Espriella deployed troops and police officers to Colombia’s border with Venezuela.

Announcing [the operation](https://www.ntn24.com/noticias-actualidad/operacion-esparta-aumenta-presion-militar-de-abelardo-de-la-espriella-contra-el-eln-en-frontera-con-venezuela-663674), Mr. De La Espriella said the troops were under orders to neutralize armed group leaders.

On a visit to the border city of Cúcuta last week, the president also [announced](https://www.instagram.com/reels/DfUz1s9sJE7/) a plan to erect barriers and surveillance infrastructure at illegal crossings along the 1,400-mile border.

Security experts said the strategy appeared to be to simultaneously target the ELN on both sides of the border and to fortify the border to prevent fighters from fleeing.

The moves immediately raised the prospect of retaliation by the ELN in the border areas that have long been their stronghold, experts said.

Image

Colombian soldiers conducted searches last month in Cúcuta. Credit...Schneyder Mendoza/Agence France-Presse — Getty Images

In addition to Saturday’s drone attack, the ELN last week [kidnapped](https://www.eltiempo.com/justicia/conflicto-y-narcotrafico/eln-confirma-el-secuestro-de-la-subteniente-del-ejercito-maria-camila-pantoja-continua-el-operativo-en-la-zona-rural-para-encontrarla-3598853) a second lieutenant in the army’s elite intelligence corps, María Camila Pantoja Hernández, in the Colombian border department of Arauca.

The ELN’s Frente de Guerra Oriental, or Eastern War Front, claimed responsibility in [a video message](https://www.infobae.com/colombia/2026/11/05/eln-confirmo-el-secuestro-de-la-subteniente-del-ejercito-maria-camila-pantoja-se-le-respetaran-sus-derechos/). A masked fighter said Lieutenant Pantoja was “doing fine.”

The ELN, which has around 6,000 fighters, is a federation of separate fronts, rather than a single group with one leader.

The episodes have set the country on edge.

Analysts say that, for the United States, having allied leaders in Colombia and Venezuela has presented a rare opportunity to pressure the ELN on both sides of the border.

Just a year ago, such an effort would have been unthinkable: Nicolás Maduro, a sworn enemy of the United States — and, according to U.S. officials, an ally of the ELN — was still Venezuela’s president.

In Colombia, the leftist president, Gustavo Petro, had [denounced](https://www.nytimes.com/2025/11/12/world/americas/gustavo-petro-colombia-trump.html) U.S. military [boat strikes](https://www.nytimes.com/interactive/2025/10/29/us/us-caribbean-pacific-boat-strikes.html) on accused drug traffickers, including the ELN, as “murder.”

Now, the U.S. has two cooperative governments.

The United States has sent equipment including [MQ-9 Reaper drones](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/10/06/world/americas/us-reaper-drones-colombia-ecuador-cartels.html) and [hundreds of troops](https://www.southcom.mil/News/PressReleases/Article/4633374/us-colombia-launch-exercise-southern-vanguard-2027/) to train with Colombian forces. Colombian officials say U.S. intelligence agencies are also helping target armed groups and their leaders.

In his September meeting with Mr. De La Espriella, Mr. Rubio made it clear that dismantling the groups was a priority for the Trump administration.

Mr. De La Espriella has appeared undeterred in that mission, even in the face of retaliatory violence. In his social media message on Saturday, he issued an explicit threat.

“For every attack, one bombardment,” he said.

Simón Posada contributed reporting from Bogotá and Isayen Herrera from Caracas.

items.title: Reeling From Rare Mass Shooting, Poles Ask What Set Off Young Suspect
items.summary: Officials say that a 24-year-old killed his family and then six people during a rampage in Krakow. Now they are trying to determine the motive.
items.full_text:
Title: Reeling From Rare Mass Shooting, Poles Ask What Set Off Young Suspect - The New York Times

URL Source: https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/08/world/europe/poland-shooting-suspect-family.html

Published Time: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 01:04:27 GMT

Markdown Content:
He lived with his parents on the top floor of a three-story apartment building painted a sunny yellow, but he nearly always dressed in black. He attended sedate family events like christenings but was fascinated by guns and the history of World War II.

A day after the authorities said a 24-year-old man had killed his sister and parents at their home and then shot dead six people in the central square of Krakow, neighbors and relatives in the gritty former steel town where the family lived were struggling to piece together what had happened. What, they asked, might have pushed an often sullen but seemingly unaggressive young man with no criminal record to mass murder?

“My legs are still shaking from shock,” said Ryszard Piasecki, who is related by marriage to the suspect’s slain mother, Renata. “He was a loner and didn’t have a girlfriend or any friends at all. He always wore black — but lots of young people do that.”

The suspect, Michal Oksinski, was a lathe operator. His parents and sister, Magdalena, a third-year student at the Fine Arts Academy in Krakow, were found late Saturday in their apartment in Ostrowiec Swietokrzyski, a Communist-era industrial center now fallen on hard times.

Magdalena, 21, was visiting for the weekend when her brother killed her on Saturday morning, according to investigators.

One Ostrowiec Swietokrzyski resident, Marta Piwowarczyk, said her brother-in-law lived in the same apartment building as the Oksinskis and called her on Saturday to say the police had sealed off the area and that “something terrible seems to have happened.”

Image

Krakow’s Main Market Square on Sunday, a day after a mass shooting.Credit...Jakub Porzycki/Reuters

After killing his family, the authorities say, Mr. Oksinski drove his father’s Subaru around 130 miles to the Old Town in Krakow. Entering its medieval central market square about 3 p.m., the height of a weekend rush in one of Poland’s most popular tourist destinations, the authorities say he began firing from the car at crowds of people strolling and shopping. Among the six people shot dead was a visitor from Britain.

Police officers, fearing that the door of the family’s home in Ostrowiec Swietokrzyski might be booby-trapped, entered the apartment late Saturday evening through a window next to a small balcony overlooking the street. On Sunday, a smashed window pane and a steady flow in and out of the building of police investigators, counterterrorism experts and forensic technicians pointed to the horrors committed there 24 hours earlier.

Americans may have grown accustomed to senseless mass murder committed by lone gunmen, but in peacetime Poland it has been met with incomprehension. “My mind can’t compute what happened. No normal person can understand what got into his empty head,” said Mr. Piasecki, the relative.

After public appeals on the day of the shooting for blood donations, the Krakow police department asked people to stop volunteering because blood banks were full. “The scale of the public response exceeded our wildest expectations,” it said Sunday.

Two police officers, among the 16 people wounded in Krakow during the rampage, were still hospitalized on Sunday. One was listed in serious condition but had emerged from the coma he was in when admitted. The Polish authorities declared two days of national mourning on Sunday and Monday.

Mr. Oksinski was shot by police officers responding to the attack. He was reported to be in critical condition.

Image

Bullet holes on a wall in Krakow’s main square a day after the shooting.Credit...Beata Zawrzel/Associated Press

The Oksinski family lived in a tidy working- and middle-class district near a small park carpeted on an autumn weekend with leaves. Mr. Oksinski’s father, Janusz, an electrician, had his own small business, and his mother worked as a cashier in a nearby food store.

After the collapse of Communism in 1989, the town’s biggest employer, a state-owned steel mill with 17,000 workers, was privatized and began slashing staff to the bone. One sign of the pain that followed endures in old graffiti daubed near the entrance to the Oksinski family’s stairwell: “Nothing is eternal.”

On Sunday, the Krakow branch of Poland’s National Prosecutor’s Office opened an investigation and [described](https://x.com/PK_GOV_PL/status/2119367536441524417) the mass shooting as an “act constituting a terrorist offense,” though it gave no hint of a possible motive.

Poland’s interior minister, Marcin Kierwinski, said it appeared to be political. “Everything points to the perpetrator holding very, very radical views,” he said. Without going into detail, he said the suspect “was fascinated by far-right ideologies.”

Local residents were not buying that.

“He wore a black hoodie and painted his nails black, but does that mean anything?” asked a retired steel mill worker, who said he used to see Mr. Oksinski in the neighborhood. He would give only his first name, Boguslaw, citing neighborhood tensions following the deaths. “Claims of a political attack is just empty talk,” he said.

Image

Police officers cordoning off an area near Krakow’s market square on Sunday.Credit...Jakub Porzycki/Reuters

His wife, Barbara, who retired from a sports club once funded by the now-moribund steel mill, said that before now she had never heard of gun violence in Ostrowiec Swietokrzyski. “When people here want to kill themselves, they jump out of windows but never use guns,” she said.

Guns, however, seem to have been a big part of Mr. Oksinski’s life.

A spokesman for the district prosecutor’s office said on Sunday that seven firearms and a large quantity of ammunition had been seized from his family’s apartment. The father, he said, had permits for nine guns, while his son had two permits. Neither had criminal records, which would have precluded the permits. Two guns were found on the son after the attack in Krakow.

Forensic experts were still working “to determine exactly which weapon was used to fire the shots in the Ostrowiec apartment,” the spokesman said.

Image

The shooting range where the suspect was reported to have practiced.Credit...Kacper Pempel/Reuters

Mr. Piasecki, the relative, said the father and son had bonded over guns, often going together on weekends to a shooting range in a nearby town. He said his wife, whose sister is related to the suspect’s mother, had shown him a picture posted weeks ago on Facebook by the young man. It portrayed him waving a gun with the caption: “Dad, thanks for buying me this.”

The gun club where they practiced firing their weapons released a statement on Sunday distancing itself from the mass shooting. It insisted that the suspect had never received “dynamic, tactical or combat shooting training at the club.” And the management, it said, “is cooperating with the authorities conducting the investigation.”

Anatol Magdziarz contributed reporting.

items.title: When the Boss on the Phone Isn’t Real: How More Than $129 Million Was Stolen Using A.I.
items.summary: A federal indictment alleges that three men used generative A.I. to impersonate voices of chief executives and lawyers to defraud companies of millions of dollars.
items.full_text:
Title: When the Boss on the Phone Isn’t Real: How More Than $129 Million Was Stolen Using A.I. - The New York Times

URL Source: https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/08/business/ai-ceo-impersonation-theft.html

Published Time: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 00:54:36 GMT

Markdown Content:
An accountant at a regional hospital system in Missouri answering the phone recognized the voice on the other end as that of the organization’s chief executive.

There was an urgent matter that required confidentiality and an immediate wire transfer, the caller said. A lawyer then quickly followed up to complete the transaction.

By the time the hospital’s actual executives realized what had happened, $4.8 million had vanished.

The executive and the lawyer never made the calls; instead, both voices had been generated by artificial intelligence, according to the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Southern District of New York.

The same script played out several times over approximately 18 months, beginning in July 2024, prosecutors said, costing companies based in the United States and Europe more than $129 million.

Attempts were also made to engage employees in video calls, deploying deepfakes of the chief executive in the scheme, prosecutors said.

Among the unnamed victims were: a British financial technology company ($11.6 million); a pet food company in Florida ($5 million); a hospital system in California ($3 million); a mutual fund company in Massachusetts ($4.7 million); and a bank based in Rhode Island ($2.7 million).

The authorities in Britain and Spain arrested Jacob Soall, Sharon Hazan and Guy Sheetrit over several months starting in June, according to an indictment unsealed on Thursday.

Mr. Soall, 41, of Marbella, Spain and Britain, was arrested in Spain. Mr. Hazan, 54, of Israel, was also arrested there. Mr. Sheetrit, 42, of Israel and the United Arab Emirates, was arrested in Britain.

The three men are awaiting extradition to the United States, where they face charges of wire fraud, aggravated identity theft and money laundering.

It was unclear whether the men have lawyers in the United States. Efforts to find contact information for them were unsuccessful.

Prosecutors said the men would send a “victim employee,” typically an accountant or finance manager, an email.

The indictment included an example of an email sent to “a major investment bank” in New York City in October 2024. The message said the employee needed to sign a nondisclosure agreement. After signing, the employee was asked to call a lawyer.

The defendants used the names of actual people at real law firms, often among the 50 largest firms in the world, to impersonate, prosecutors said.

Only a few years ago, a bad actor needed hours upon hours of audio to mimic a voice, said [Hany Farid](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/06/14/us/ai-deepfake-hany-farid.html), a Dartmouth College computer science professor and chief science officer at GetReal Security, a cybersecurity company that guards against A.I.-powered identity attacks and deepfakes.

That left chief executives and public-facing lawyers — with hours of high-fidelity audio online via earnings calls, keynotes and media appearances — as targets.

Now we are all potential targets, he said.

“I would comfortably say with less than a minute, you can clone somebody,” Dr. Farid said on Sunday.

Instead of needing thousands of images of somebody with different head poses, lighting and camera angles to capture their facial geometry, all that is needed is a single photo to create an “avatar deepfake,” he said.

The software for this is easy to use and newer laptops can keep up with the necessary computational demand, Dr. Farid said.

While many people claim to be able to tell the difference, Dr. Farid said his studies had shown otherwise.

“People are just slightly above chance performance,” he said. “So they’re really, really bad at it.”

Federal prosecutors said the men directed the victims to wire money to bank accounts controlled by conspirators across the world, including in Austria, China, Greece, Portugal, Singapore, Slovakia, Spain, the United Arab Emirates and the United States.

After the money had been wired, the men and co-conspirators converted it into cryptocurrency, the U.S. Attorney’s Office said, to try to conceal the source, ownership and control of the stolen money, while distributing it among themselves.

Mr. Soall kept a handwritten script, “Lawyer Call,” that he used when speaking with victims, the prosecutors said, including language to help persuade the employees not to discuss their communications with colleagues.

The script used regulatory jargon and insider trading risks as a pretext for strict secrecy, according to the indictment.

Mr. Hazan and Mr. Sheetrit laundered funds from the fraud scheme, among other activities, officials said.

Mr. Hazan bragged that he had laundered more than $400 million in the last three years.

Among themselves, Mr. Soall used the alias “Rocky Balboa” and Mr. Hazan went by “Superman Cash” and “Fat Boy,” among others, prosecutors said.

The F.B.I. Internet Crime Complaint Center’s [2025 report](https://www.ic3.gov/AnnualReport/Reports/2025_IC3Report.pdf) highlighted a surge in digital fraud and cyberthreats. Total complaints surpassed one million for the first time, while total losses surpassed $20 billion, a 26 percent increase in losses compared with 2024.

The agency logged more than 22,000 complaints related to artificial intelligence, totaling over $890 million in losses. Those schemes used generative A.I. to create realistic phishing emails, clone voices for family emergency/distress scams and enhance romance fraud scripts, it said.

Dr. Farid said that through his company he speaks with company executives who are struggling with everything from fake remote interviews to multimillion-dollar scams.

“I had one C.E.O. tell me a couple of months ago, ‘That’s it, we’re doing everything in person,’” he said.
